title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When it comes to pregnancy, a healthy diet plays a crucial role in ensuring the well-being of both mother and baby. Iron and folate are two essential nutrients that are vital for the development of the fetus. In this article, we will introduce three delicious and nutritious recipes that combine iron and folate, which can be cooked in under 30 minutes.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two critical nutrients during pregnancy. Iron helps produce hemoglobin, a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen to the body's tissues. Folate helps prevent birth defects of the brain and spine. To enhance iron absorption, it's recommended to combine iron-rich foods with vitamin C-rich foods.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl with Lime
* 100g grilled chicken
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup steamed broccoli
* 1 lime
* Note: Choose chicken that has been cooked thoroughly and broccoli that has been washed clean.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry Bowl with Bell Peppers
* 100g beef stir-fry
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup sautéed bell peppers
* 1 tablespoon soy sauce
* Note: Choose beef that has been cooked thoroughly and bell peppers that have been washed clean.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Bowl with Tofu and Mixed Greens
* 100g pan-fried tofu
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed greens
* 1 tablespoon lemon juice
* Note: Choose tofu that has been cooked thoroughly and mixed greens that have been washed clean.

## Practical Tips
* Choose fresh and nutritious ingredients to ensure food safety.
* Cook food thoroughly to avoid foodborne illness.
* Combine iron-rich foods with vitamin C-rich foods to enhance iron absorption.
* For more delicious and nutritious recipe ideas, visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner).

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about your diet during pregnancy, consult your healthcare provider or a registered dietitian.
